Standard and decorative light bulbs supply the light source for a variety of fixtures in offices, hospitality settings, residential buildings, and more.
Spot, reflector, and flood light bulbs intensify their light output by reflecting light away from the bulb sides and directing it through the top.
Miniature light bulbs typically fit into tight spaces for specialized lighting applications.
Plug-in CFL and LED light bulbs have a pin base that fits a matching socket on a compatible light fixture.
U-bend lights bulbs fit their arched tube into troffers and other fixtures with limited bulb space while providing illumination similar to linear lamps.
Circular light bulbs emit a full circle of light for uniform distribution in general lighting applications.
Light bulb and lamp accessories hold lamps in place, assist with lamp removal and installation, and enhance or restore lamp function.
Ballasts and drivers install into lighting fixtures to regulate current and voltage flowing to the fixtures' lamps or LED arrays.
Fluorescent ballasts install into compatible lighting fixtures to protect linear fluorescent and CFL lamps from damaging power fluctuations that affect the lamp's output quality.
HID (High-Intensity Discharge) ballasts pair with lighting fixtures that use metal-halide or high pressure sodium HID lamps.
LED drivers protect lamps from damaging fluctuations in the power supply that can reduce the quality of lamps' or arrays' light output.
Emergency lighting ballasts and drivers keep light fixtures on during a power outage.
Lighting fixtures and retrofit kits hard-wire into an electrical system or plug into outlets to supply indoor illumination.
Surface mount lights attach directly to ceilings or walls to supply general lighting in workplaces, healthcare settings, and retail spaces.
Panel and troffer light fixtures mount in drop ceiling grids to provide general lighting for large open areas and hallways.
Bay lights deliver bright, uniform illumination from high ceilings or open trusses to floors and work surfaces below.
Can lights and downlights cast a narrow light beam downward for general lighting or accent lighting.
Vapor-tight lights prevent dust and moisture from entering the fixture and damaging internal wiring and components.

Vandal-resistant and confinement light fixtures resist impacts and tampering to illuminate behavior health facilities, schools, transit centers, public restrooms, and other indoor spaces with a higher risk of damage.
Hazardous location light fixtures illuminate areas with flammable, combustible, or ignitable materials.
Healthcare light fixtures illuminate hospitals, clinics, nursing homes, animal care facilities, and other medical and personal care settings.
Disinfecting and sanitizing UV light fixtures produce UV-A or UV-C rays to decontaminate surfaces or air.
Track light fixtures serve as accent lights or spotlights to illuminate small spaces, highlight product displays or decorative features, and brighten corners and alcoves.
Under-cabinet and accent lights supplement general lighting, provide task lighting, or highlight specific areas or features.
Decorative light fixtures supply illumination and add visual interest for general and accent lighting in retail, hospitality, office, healthcare, and multifamily housing settings.
LED rope and tape lights supply a strip of light for long runs and decorative trims in accent lighting applications.
Grow lights emit light in color spectrums that optimize seedling growth, stem and leaf growth, or budding and flowering to grow plants indoors.
Night lights provide low-level illumination to help light darkened rooms, hallways, and pathways for safety and orientation.
Outdoor lighting fixtures withstand weather exposure, illuminating outdoor areas or partially exposed locations.
Wall packs and decorative wall lights mount flush on exterior walls to uniformly illuminate building features, increase pedestrian visibility, and help deter crime.

Floodlights project a high-output beam to spotlight fixed objects like a monument or flagpole or increase visibility and security in larger dim or dark areas such as parks, building exteriors, loading docks, driveways, and parking lots.
Street and parking lot lights, also known as area and site lights, emit elevated bright light from sunset to sunrise to enhance visibility and safety in roadways and parking lots.
Landscape lights illuminate outdoor spaces to increase visibility, prevent accidents, and draw attention to landscaped areas such as lawns, gardens, and planting beds.
Security lights illuminate perimeters, doorways, and other outdoor areas around buildings, residences, and garages to help deter theft and vandalism at night.
Solar lights convert sunlight to electricity to illuminate outdoor areas, reduce energy costs, and eliminate the need for a power supply.
Outdoor lampholders increase visibility and provide safe navigation for pedestrians.
Parks and recreation lights illuminate large areas such as outdoor parks and recreational facilities, municipal fields, courts, and open-air venues.
Emergency and exit lighting provides illumination and direction to guide people out of buildings during a power loss or other emergency.
Emergency light fixtures automatically switch on when power goes out and illuminate pathways toward exits.
Remote head emergency lights supplement illumination from primary emergency lighting in the event of a power loss.
Combination exit signs with emergency lights are all-in-one fixtures that mark exits and illuminate pathways to guide evacuations from buildings.
Lighted exit signs hardwire into an electrical system that keeps them lit for visibility.
These retrofit kits convert lighted exit signs from incandescent or halogen to LED.
Emergency lighting accessories and batteries maintain or enhance the performance of emergency lights and exit signs.
Task and jobsite lighting offers temporary illumination to brighten unlit spaces and supplement general lighting for construction, assembly, maintenance, and other work.
Hand lamps spread light over a wide area when hung by their hook or magnet, or they direct light like a flashlight when held by hand.
Jobsite lights cast light into workspaces and onto work surfaces, providing more focused illumination than 360-degree jobsite lights in areas where general lighting is inadequate or unavailable.
360-degree jobsite lights emit a full circle of light to distribute illumination across a room or large space where multiple people are working.
Remote area lights supply portable, temporary floodlighting at emergency scenes, construction sites, sporting events, and other outlying or isolated locations that require lots of bright light.
Hanging and string lights deliver light from above to supply temporary or semi-permanent area and task lighting for construction, assembly, maintenance, and other jobs.
Dock lights mount to a wall or post and extend their light head on a movable arm to shine light into trailers and onto loading docks or staging areas.
Workstation lights focus light onto benchtops, desktops, and other work surfaces.
Machine tool lights mount in, on, or near machining, manufacturing, and fabrication equipment to brighten obscured areas and supply targeted illumination for placing and examining work.
Flashlights are portable light sources that temporarily supplement fixtures or illuminate areas where other lighting is unavailable or impractical.
Handheld flashlights supply personal, portable lighting to navigate dark or dimly lit areas.
Headlamps and helmet lights are worn on a worker's head, making them visible to others in dark spaces, illuminating their area of focus, and keeping both hands free to work.
Penlights and inspection lights shine a small, focused light beam onto specific areas or into tight spaces where flashlights would be too large or overpowering.
Right-angle flashlights angle their head at 90° from their body, aiming light beams straight ahead when clipped in place or held upright.
Lanterns and spotlights provide more illumination than flashlights, shining light over a wider area or at greater distances.
Weapon-mounted flashlights attach to firearms and provide illumination for accurate targeting.
These flashlights crank by hand, plug in to stay charged, or draw power from water, making them ready for use during power outages without the worry of depleted batteries.
Clip and keychain flashlights are lightweight, compact, and remain close at hand for when illumination is needed.
Flashlight parts and accessories adapt flashlights for specific applications, keep them powered up, or restore their function.
Lighting controls dim, turn on, and turn off lighting to manage usage and reduce energy costs.
Lighting dimmers decrease light output from its maximum setting to adjust brightness.
Occupancy sensors monitor a room and automatically switch off lights after occupants leave the room.
These accessories customize operation and assist with installation of lighting control systems.
Light bulb crushers pulverize dead or broken fluorescent bulbs to minimize the space required for storing them, and they have filters that capture contaminants released during the crushing process.
Lighting replacement parts are used to repair or enhance the utility of light fixtures.
Lamp replacement parts repair worn or damaged components or enhance the utility of lamps.

Lubrication keeps motors, tools, and mechanical equipment running smoothly by reducing friction, inhibiting heat, and preventing corrosion which increases operation efficiency and prolongs equipment life.
Grease lubricates moving parts, inhibits heat, and seals out contaminants in equipment and machinery.
Multipurpose grease lubricates many different types of equipment in a variety of industrial operations without the need for a specialized grease.
Food-grade multipurpose grease lubricates machine parts and equipment in food, beverage, and pharmaceutical production facilities.
Bearing grease lubricates the balls, rollers, and cylindrical-shaped elements that move together to support and align rotating parts.

Food-grade bearing grease lubricates balls, rollers, and cylindrical-shaped elements that move together to support and align rotating parts in food, beverage, and pharmaceutical processing equipment and machinery.
O-ring grease lubricates, seals, and conditions O-rings in valve system components to ensure a seal and protect the system against moisture, heat, and oxidation.
Open gear grease is a thick paste-type lubricant designed to stay in place on exposed, slow-moving gears and bearings.
Plumbing grease is a water-resistant lubricant designed for plumbing fixtures such as faucets to reduce stiffness, squeaking, and to extend the life of moving parts.
Oils inhibit heat, reduce friction, and prevent wear on moving parts.
Hydraulic oils, also called hydraulic fluids, circulate through pressurized systems to lubricate and transmit power.

Food-grade hydraulic oils, also called hydraulic fluids, circulate through pressurized systems to lubricate and transmit power in food, beverage, and pharmaceutical production equipment and machinery.
Circulating oils provide a continuous, reusable supply of lubrication to gears, bearings, and other components in industrial machinery.
Gear oils lubricate, cool, and protect gear teeth that slide and roll together under high pressures and speeds.
Food-grade gear oils lubricate, cool, and protect gear teeth in processing equipment for food, beverage, and pharmaceutical production facilities.
Machine oils lubricate moving or threaded parts in a variety of machines and equipment to reduce friction, prevent corrosion, and extend the working life of components.
Food-grade machine oils lubricate machine parts and equipment in food, beverage, and pharmaceutical production facilities.
Food-grade divider oils lubricate food processing equipment and provide a releasing agent to prevent residual food from sticking to equipment.
Way oils reduce friction between sliding parts to help prevent wear on the parts and allow them to move smoothly.
Spindle oils lubricate machine spindles and withstand degradation when used in high-speed applications.
Lubricants and penetrating lubricants add a slippery film or coating on machinery, tools, and parts to reduce wear and friction between surfaces and keep equipment running smoothly.
Lubricants reduce friction, wear, and overheating in mechanical equipment by coating surfaces with a slippery fluid that smooths the movement of parts and extends machine life.
Dry lubricants reduce friction between moving parts without leaving a messy wet residue that attracts dirt and debris.
Penetrating lubricants loosen stuck or frozen fasteners and bolts to remove them from equipment or machinery.
Anti-seize compounds prevent assembled parts and fasteners from sticking together or corroding to ensure they can be dismantled for maintenance and repairs without shearing or needing to be cut off.
Mold release agents are applied directly to molds to create a barrier that prevents materials from sticking to them.
Grease guns apply grease directly in locations where a permanent lubrication system is not practical such as on automobiles, farm equipment, aircraft, and wind turbines.
Manual grease guns dispense grease with a simple, hand-powered operation.
Battery-powered grease guns can be maneuvered freely around confined, elevated, or remote areas without the need for a wired power source.
Air-operated grease guns use compressed air to deliver a consistent flow of lubricant.
These items replace worn or damaged hoses, pipes, and barrels on grease guns.
Couplers, also called dispensing tips, attach to the end of a grease gun's nozzle, hose, or pipe where lubrication is discharged.
These accessories support the operation and handling of grease guns.
Grease fittings (zerk fittings) install permanently in equipment to provide entry points for delivering grease to components such as bearings and gears.
Grease fittings (zerk fittings) are permanently installed entry points on equipment for delivering grease to components such as bearings and gears without overflow or leaks.
Adapters and manifolds alter grease fittings and consolidate multiple lubrication points to expedite and support lubrication on heavy equipment and industrial machinery.
Washers, caps, and tools support the use and maintenance of grease fittings (zerk fittings).
Handheld oilers and oil measuring containers are simple, economical devices that help with the measurement and dispensing of oil.
Handheld oil dispensers are simple, economical oilers that provide controlled delivery of small amounts of oil with a one-handed operation.
Oil measuring containers assist with handheld measuring and transferring of lubricants.
Machine-mount lubricators automatically dispense grease or oil to critical components such as bearings, slides, gears, and chains to avoid equipment breakdown or malfunction.
Single-point grease lubricators mount to machines to automatically dispense grease onto bearings and other moving machine parts to keep them lubricated without the need for manual inspections.
Service kits for single-point grease lubricators include grease refill and components to maintain lubricators when the grease supply is replenished.
Constant-level and drip-feed oilers ensure moving parts have a steady feed of lubrication as oil levels deplete over time due to displacement, misting, and evaporation.
These accessories support the operation and maintenance of constant-level and drip-feed oilers.
Lubrication systems apply oil and grease to working machinery to keep parts moving efficiently and reduce maintenance and system downtime.
Oil storage and dispensing systems seal, organize, identify, and provide controlled dispensing of lubricants.
Oil storage containers and transfer lids keep lubricants sealed, separated, organized, and protected from contaminants in containers that are sized for hand-carrying around a shop floor.
Extension hoses and hand pumps help dispense oil from storage containers.
Bulk oil storage tanks and dispensing systems offer solutions for the delivery and storage of oil in facilities with heavy oil usage.
Desiccant breathers and breather vents ensure the flow of clean air in closed lubrication systems to prevent pressure or vacuum.

Desiccant breathers mount to lubrication containers or reservoirs in industrial equipment to allow clean, dry air to flow into the system, keeping pressure neutral while preventing the ingress of moisture or contaminants.
Breather vents prevent unexpected pressure or vacuum changes in closed systems by allowing the exchange of air with the atmosphere.

Level gauges, flow sights, and viewports mount externally onto equipment and allow visual checks and monitoring of lubricant levels, flow, and condition in closed systems where direct contact and testing of lubricants is not practical.
Oil level gauges mount externally to equipment for visual checks and monitoring of lubricant levels.
Lubricant flow sights and viewports allow monitoring of lubricant flow, condition, and clarity in closed systems where direct contact and testing of lubricant is not practical.
Machining is a process in which material is removed from a workpiece to shape or finish it into a desired form.
Drilling and holemaking tools create and finish holes in a workpiece.
Drill bits have cutting edges that remove material as they are rotated and fed into a workpiece by handheld drills, drill presses, or CNC machines.
Reamers enlarge or finish an existing hole to a precise size with a smooth surface.
Countersinks, center drills, and spotting drills create shallow holes in workpieces, each with specific purposes in the holemaking process.
Counterbores and port tools expand existing holes for a precise fit when installing fasteners or ports.
Broaches are used to machine keyways, splines, and other shapes into a hole in metalworking tasks.
Punches and dies make holes in sheet metal.

Drill bushings (also known as jig bushings) install in a drilling jig to guide, position, and support drill bits, reamers, countersinks, and counterbores to ensure accurate and repeatable hole placement in metalworking tasks.
Drill bit extensions attach to drill bits to extend the bits' reach and allow them to drill deep holes.

Holemaking blanks are metal rods that can be machined to create custom drill bits, reamers, or other round cutting tools with precise dimensions or features to suit a particular metalworking application.
Milling is a machining process in which a rotating cutting tool removes material from the surface of a workpiece.
End mills have cutting edges on their nose and sides that remove material from the surface of a piece of stock.
CNC router bits install in milling machines and CNC routers to make plunge and profile cuts in solid surfaces.
Engraving tools have a pointed tip that cuts letters, numbers, and designs into a variety of metals and composites.
Milling cutters have teeth that remove material from a piece of stock to create parts with complex features and shapes.
Mold and die milling tools have tapered sides that allow them to fit into the channels in a mold or die.
Threading is a machining process in which a tool is used to create threads on the external or internal surface of a fastener, part, or workpiece.
Taps are cylindrical tools that create internal threads for connection with compatible fasteners.
Dies create or repair external threads on cylindrical parts like rods, pipe, or fasteners that insert into holes with corresponding internal threads.
Threading sets include multiple taps, dies, and drill bits in a range of sizes, eliminating the need to buy threading tools separately.
Tap and die accessories support the operation and maintenance of taps and dies.
Thread repair tools fix damaged threads and restore them to their original condition.
Thread mills cut internal and external threads into a hole or the surface of a part.
Turning, boring, and grooving are machining operations that remove material from workpieces.
Boring bars are single-point cutting tools used with lathes, CNC lathes, turning machines, and machining centers to size, straighten, and finish the inside diameter of drilled or cast holes.
Internal threading tools are single-point cutting tools used with lathes, CNC lathes, or turning machines to add internal threads to drilled or cast holes in workpieces.
Knurling tools are wheeled cutting tools used with lathes to create textured surfaces on workpieces.
Lathe tool bits, blanks, and sets are used on lathes to perform turning, boring, grooving, and threading operations.
Turning and grooving tools are used with lathes to remove sections of material or add grooves to workpieces.
Indexable cutting tools perform like traditional cutting tools but have a tool body or toolholder that accepts replaceable indexable inserts or exchangeable heads to form a cutting edge.
Indexable boring tools are used with lathes or CNC turning machines to remove material from inside holes.
These milling tools have a tool body or toolholder that accepts replaceable cutting heads or indexable inserts to form a cutting edge.
Indexable and modular drilling and holemaking tools have a tool body or toolholder that accepts replaceable indexable inserts or exchangeable heads to form a cutting edge.
Indexable parting and grooving tools are used with lathes or CNC turning machines to remove sections of a workpiece in parting or cut-off operations or add grooves to a workpiece.
Indexable threading is a machining process that uses replaceable cutting inserts to add internal or external threads to a workpiece.
Indexable turning tools are used with lathes or CNC turning machines to remove material from workpieces in order to size, shape, and add features to them.
These replacement parts and accessories restore or improve the function of indexable cutting tools to avoid the expense of replacing the entire toolholder.
Machinery is used in metal shops and production facilities to shape and finish parts in machining operations.
Buffing and grinding machines finish, shape, and remove material from workpieces.
Drill presses and magnetic drills have a vertical drill head mounted to a base that provides stability and maintains consistent alignment to make more uniform holes than handheld drills.
Hydraulic presses and accessories bend, straighten, flatten, or stamp workpieces.
Lathe machines cut, shape, size, or finish cylindrical workpieces.
Metal fabrication machines shape or cut metal workpieces.
Milling machines use rotary cutting tools to shape workpieces, add grooves and contoured shoulders, and create parts with complex shapes and features in manufacturing plants and machine shops.
Marking machines use lasers or replaceable percussive tips to etch text or images permanently and precisely onto surfaces.
Waterjet cutting machines use high-pressure streams of water to shape or cut metal, glass, granite, ceramic, plastic, or other materials.
Metal dust collection and air filtration keep workspaces and ambient air clean in metal shops and metal fabrication applications.
Machine bases raise tools or equipment (such as bench lathes, milling machines, or drills) off the floor to position them at proper heights for operation or to reposition them in the workspace.
Machine leveling components incrementally raise and lower machine parts, benches, or bases to level, align, and position them.
Storage baskets keep machining parts and supplies organized and out of the way.
Toolholders and tooling systems attach cutting tools to machine tools, such as CNCs and lathes.
Drill chucks and accessories work with drill presses, milling machines, and lathes to grip drill bits, taps, and other cutting tools for milling and tapping applications.
Collets and accessories hold small-diameter cutting tools or workpieces on a milling machine, lathe, or other machine tool.
Collet chucks mount collets onto milling machines, lathes, and other manual and CNC machine tools so that the collets can hold small-diameter tools and workpieces securely on the machine.
Tapping heads and holders connect taps to drilling and milling machines to create threads in holes.
Lathe tool posts and tool post holders support cutting tools on manual or CNC metalworking lathes.
End mill holders, adapters, and accessories connect rotary cutting tools (such as drills and end mills) to a milling machine.
Milling chucks lock end mills onto a milling machine for accurate, high-speed machining.
Face mill holders mount a face mill to a milling machine or a CNC machining center.
Shell mill holders secure shell mills and face mills to a milling machine.
Boring heads and holders connect boring tools to milling machines, lathes, or other machines.
Rotary broach holders and set-up plugs improve the accuracy of rotary broaches, which produce polygonal shapes in holes.
Rotary toolholder retention knobs thread into the shank of a tapered toolholder to provide a pull stud for a milling machine's drawbar to grab.
CNC toolholder tightening fixtures mount to a benchtop to provide a stable workstation for attaching tools and collets to toolholders.
CNC toolholder storage products keep equipment organized and protect it from bumps that can damage cutting edges.
Clamping, workholding, and positioning products hold workpieces in place and adjust components in woodworking, machining, and production operations.
Manual toggle and hold-down clamps secure and position parts, workpieces, and materials for fastening, assembly, metal fabrication, woodworking, and other processes.
Air-powered swing and toggle clamps use compressed air rather than mechanical force to apply clamping pressure to hold workpieces in place.
Machine table clamps and hardware secure workpieces to holes and slots in worktables.
Fixture clamps have a low-profile clamp block that presses onto the end of a workpiece to secure it to a worktable.
Machine vises and accessories are used on machine worktables to position and hold workpieces during machining.
Indexing and positioning equipment sets up parts and workpieces for layout, inspection, and machining.
Lathe centers, chucks, and jaws center and support workpieces between the headstock and tailstock to provide accurate milling.
Stationary fixturing tools provide high stability to ensure high levels of precision for critical machining applications, including layout and inspection tasks.
Precision measuring tools measure dimensions of workpieces, parts, or features for a variety of applications, including quality assurance inspections.
Calipers and accessories measure thickness, length, diameter, and depth of workpieces, machined parts, or features.
Micrometers perform outside, inside, depth, or specialty measurements at a higher level of precision than calipers.
Height gauges verify workpiece height in metalworking or metrology applications.
Indicators amplify a displacement or change in value from a nominal zero point.
Pin, plug, and ring gauges test plain or threaded parts to determine if they are within acceptable tolerance ranges of the nominal specified size.
Inside diameter gauges perform precise direct or indirect measurements on holes or bores.
Inspection and calibration tools and equipment are used for quality assurance before, during, and after production on the shop floor or in a dedicated QA or metrology lab.
Magnification instruments examine and measure small parts, objects, or text.
These kits contain tools to support a variety of precision measuring applications.
Protractors and machinist squares and sets are measuring tools for finding angles in layout, setup applications, and determining inclines.
Quick-check reference gauges verify the sizes and tolerances of parts.
Setup, layout, and alignment tools are used for positioning, layout, setup, and alignment applications.
Surface property testing checks the characteristics of a surface to ensure parts or workpieces are manufactured within acceptable parameters.
Thickness gauges and feeler gauges measure the thickness of a part or the gaps between openings or parts.
SPC components pair with precision measuring tools that have SPC output capability to record and transfer data to a personal computer.
Coordinate measuring machines (CMMs) pair with probes and accessories to inspect and measure objects autonomously.
Metalworking fluids are used in machining operations to smooth cutting tasks, extend tool life, and keep equipment clean.

Cutting fluids are used in metalworking and machining applications to lubricate the cutting tool and metal workpiece to keep surfaces cool and carry away swarf and chips to limit tool wear and produce a better finish.
Machining fluid additives are used along with coolant system lubricants, oils, or coolants to improve fluid life and reduce machine maintenance.
Layout fluids reduce glare and create contrasting backgrounds that show scribed lines on workpieces during machining.
Machine tool sump cleaners remove impurities between fluid changes to speed cleaning and remove residue in supply lines and machine surfaces.
Electrical-discharge machining (EDM) fluids are used in sinker EDM operations to create highly accurate, precise cuts on workpieces.
Machining coolant systems move air and coolant through hoses to a cutting tool to limit heat buildup that can dull tools and damage sensitive components.
Mist coolant systems attach to machining equipment to spray a light covering of coolant onto tools and workpieces during cutting or machining operations.
Flood coolant systems attach to machine tools (such as lathes, CNCs, and grinders) to provide a constant coolant stream to a workpiece during high-speed, high-feed, or long-cycle cutting operations.

Minimum-quantity lubrication (MQL) systems lubricate workpieces and cutting tool edges to keep workpieces and tools cool, improve workpiece quality, extend cutting tool life, and move swarf away from the workpiece.
Cold-air coolant systems produce cold air to keep workpieces and cutting tool edges cool.
Coolant mixers automatically blend coolant concentrate with water and dispense a specific ratio of coolant to water to a coolant sump, tank, or reservoir for use in industrial machining environments.
Coolant nozzles install on machine tool coolant tanks to dispense fluid directly onto the workpiece and cutting tool to keep cutting edges cool, improve workpiece quality, and extend tool life.
Flexible-mount coolant shields protect workers from spray, mist, and light chips.
Oil skimmers and coalescers remove tramp oils from coolant tanks and parts washers.
Coolant cleaner vacuums remove chips and swarf from cutting fluids in parts washers, sumps, and tanks.
Coolant system filtration circulates coolants and machining fluids remove contaminants, protect pumps and downstream equipment, improve heat transfer, and extend tool life.
Machine tool coolant pumps circulate coolant through a machine cutting system to prevent cutting tools from overheating during operation.
Tool blanks are unground pieces of material that can be formed into custom tool bits.
3D printing is used in manufacturing to create parts, molds, prototypes, and tools.
3D printers deposit thin layers of filament on top of each other that then fuse to form a 3D object.
3D-printing filament is fed into a 3D printer to provide material for making objects.
3D printing resin is used in compatible resin 3D printers to produce high-quality models, prototypes, and parts.
3D-printing accessories are used with 3D printers to improve speed and efficiency during printing processes.
Injection molding is a manufacturing process used to produce plastic parts.
Injection molding ejector and core pins are components of injection molding systems that produce plastic parts.
Injection molding locking and stopping components keep injection molding systems running smoothly and protect them from damage.
Injection molding leader pins and ejector bushings help ensure consistent operation during injection molding processes.
Injection molding support pillars provide additional support to cavities, sprue, and runner systems within injection molds.
Material handling equipment makes it easier to move, store, and handle materials and cargo.
Ladders, platforms, and scaffolding provide elevated access to reach areas above the ground.
Step stools are small, compact, and feature one or more steps that provide extra height to reach elevated spaces and perform tasks off the ground.
Ladders provide access to elevated and hard-to-reach areas.
Stairs provide access up or down from one level to another.
Work platforms raise people to optimal heights to increase productivity and reduce the risk of back injuries and fatigue while performing tasks for long periods of time.
Platforms and mezzanines offer extra height for storage, work, security, or improved traffic flow in a facility.
Elevated safety gates install across openings in railings and guardrails to help prevent people or equipment from falling through the openings.
Scaffolding is a temporary structure that provides an elevated platform for workers to stand on and hold their equipment and materials while they perform tasks.
Personnel lifts elevate to different heights and have platforms for workers to stand on while performing overhead tasks like maintenance, repairs, and installations.
Dock equipment supports the loading and unloading of goods from vehicle trailers in loading docks, yards, and similar areas in industrial facilities.
Rail yard equipment includes tools and supplies used to support daily operations, maintenance, and safety in active rail yard environments.
Wheel chocks wedge in front of and behind vehicle wheels to prevent the vehicle from moving during maintenance or storage.
Trailer-stabilizing jacks install underneath the front end of a semitrailer to support the trailer when it's parked and not connected to a tractor.
Loading ramps, plates, and boards ease transitions between loading docks and trailers or provide a path to load and unload cargo.
Dock bumpers absorb impact and protect structures and trucks from damage during deliveries.

Dock seals and shelters install around loading dock doors to protect cargo, contain heated or cooled air, and keep hazards and particulates (such as wind, rain, and exhaust fumes) out of buildings and trucks.
Dock doors and curtains prevent unauthorized personnel access while keeping dirt and debris from entering the building.
Dock door safety nets are temporary barriers that restrict access to loading dock doors while still allowing air to circulate.
Trailer curtains and strip doors install in trucks and trailers to reduce noise and keep out bugs and debris.
Wheel risers elevate trucks so the gate is level with the loading dock to allow cargo to be loaded and unloaded safely.
Clearance bars suspend over a driveway or under a building entrance to alert drivers to the maximum allowed height in a parking garage or other structure.
Guardrails, handrails, and column, corner, and wall protectors prevent damage to structures and help people safely navigate a facility.
Guardrails protect buildings and equipment and separate spaces designed for vehicle and foot traffic.
Handrails attach to the ground or another stable surface (such as a wheelchair ramp) to provide stability and keep pedestrians, wheelchairs, and scooters within a safe walkway.
Column protectors absorb energy to limit structural damage caused when forklifts and other equipment make contact with structural columns.
Corner and wall protectors limit light structural and vehicle damage caused when vehicles, pallet jacks, and hand trucks make contact with building walls, edges, and corners.
Lifting, pulling, and positioning items attach to materials, equipment, and objects to secure and move them.
Tongs are used to grip and lift heavy items, such as railroad ties.
Hoists and trolleys transport and position heavy and large loads.
Cranes and festoon cable systems lift and position loads and provide power to hoists.
Winches revolve cable or rope around drums to generate pulling forces that move heavy loads horizontally and/or vertically.
Lift tables, turntables, and pallet positioners bring loads closer to workers, improving ergonomics and efficiency.
Box dumpers secure and lift containers, boxes, and crates to empty their contents into machinery, conveyors, chutes, and other containers.
Drywall lifts help install ceiling and wall panels.
Lifting and rigging hardware connect various types of components to support moving and securing loads.
Chains connect with loads to tow, rig, secure, and move them.
Lifting slings secure loads to move and position them overhead.
Rope and twine are cords made from braided and unbraided natural or synthetic materials.
Wire rope and fittings secure heavy loads to hoist, position, tow, and rig them using lifting and rigging equipment.
Below-the-hook lifting devices attach to cranes, hoists, or other lifting equipment to lift, position, and transport loads.
Suction lifters utilize suction cups to create vacuum forces that grip loads to lift, move, or position them where needed.
Lifting magnets move, lift, and position metal sheets, parts, and objects for manual and automated processes.
Push-pull jacks are mechanical jacks used for pushing, pulling, and holding in construction and engineering applications.
Load securing and cargo control products install on trailers, trucks, and vehicles to protect shipments and contents during transport.
Ratchet straps and cam straps wrap around cargo and connect to an anchor point on a truck or trailer bed to secure loads and prevent shifting during transport.
Winch straps and tie-down winches work together to secure heavy cargo loads to flatbed trailers.
Bungee cords, straps, and balls are flexible and stretch to secure cargo and hold bundles together.
Rope tie-downs secure light loads between two secure anchor points.
Cargo corner protectors install between a tie-down and the load to prevent damage to tie-downs or cargo.
Load binders for chain tie-downs tighten chain between the anchor points.
Load and cargo bars support and restrain pallets, boxes, and stacked cargo.
Cargo nets secure large, irregular loads in truck beds, inside vehicles, and on trailers.
Truck and trailer anchors for tie-downs provide a secure attachment point for winches, bungee cords, and ratchet and cam straps.
